ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
Ind. Code  ch. 8-1-26  provides  the  procedure for  the Indiana  Utility  Regulatory 
Commission’s Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”) to find violations  of said  chapter. Upon 
review of  those findings,  the Indiana  Underground  Plant  Protection Advisory  Committee 
(“Advisory Committee”) reviews those recommendations and recommends civil penalties in the 
Case.   
The Cases received pursuant to Ind. Code ch. 8-1- 26 and ripe for Commiss ion action are 
attached hereto and collectively referred to as the Advisory Committee Recommendations.  
Pursuant to statute, the Advisory Committee has submitted their recommendations  to the 
Commission. The Commission  UPHOLDS the findings  of violations  by  the Pipeline  Safety 
Division and APPROVES  the recommendations  of the Advisory  Committee  as  listed on the 
attached pages. The Assistant General Counsel to  the Division  is directed  to prepare  and send 
notice to the parties advising them of the determination. 
Any approve d civil penalt ies are due withi n 90 days of the date of this Order unless 
payment arrangements are made with the Secretary of the Commission.   
Any approved trainings must be comple ted no late r than 180 day s from the date of this 
Order or the alternative civil penalty noted in the attached recommendation is due.   
IT IS SO ORDERED. 
HUSTON, FREEMAN, KREVDA, OBER, AND ZIEGNER CONCUR:

Dana Kosco

**Results (by order year, using the order date in each file name):**

- **2021: 41.3%** (662 of 1,603 cases have a recorded abstention)
- **2024: 54.0%** (1,025 of 1,897 cases)
- **2025: 49.8%** (838 of 1,684 cases)

**Method:** I counted cases as "Case Number:" lines in each order's text. For each case, I counted the Abstentions field as recorded when the text after "Abstentions:" was not blank and not just the leaked "Additional Information:" phrase. Every case in these three years has exactly one Abstentions field. No abstention text was found on the line after a blank field, and the leaked phrase never appeared on the same line as real abstention text.

**Caveats:**
- Order dates come from the file names (for example, `ord_PSD_121521` is treated as 12/15/2021), because the order text does not print a date I could find. The 58 files split into 11 for 2021, 11 for 2024, 10 for 2025, plus 26 in 2022–2023, which matches the 58-order count.
- I could not run a script, so the counts come from regex searches over the extracted text files, not from a parsed dataset. The per-file totals reconcile: the case count matches the Abstentions-line count in every file.
